directExclusions.reason: An unqualified tree or plant label can describe the tree. 植える's displayed plant lacks a visible verb marker and must be guarded directly, not transitively through 植物. Different specific tree species are not equivalents. No broad timber/material clique: the exact primary family names the tree, and the article identifies the material compound 桐材 explicitly.

Direct tree and unqualified plant-label safeguards, not taxonomy-based equivalence between every related plant word. Whole-family astronomical りゅう is distinguished; it does not turn the ordinary tree into every star/sky label.

Poem/verse are broad fitting labels; the actual senryu dictionary gloss comic haiku motivates a conservative direct haiku guard without asserting identical Japanese traditions. Written-form-only meaning questions also admit the separate riverside-willow and tea senses even though the article's primary kana is せんりゅう: protect direct willow/tree/plant and both existing tea-titled cards. Tea pair exclusions are not transitive and exact-title deduplication between 茶/お茶 does not protect 川柳 against either.
